metadata.name: Hypothyroidism
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but myxoedema coma is a rare emergency
metadata.severity: Usually mild-moderate and easily treated; subclinical to overt to (rarely) myxoedema coma

overview.short_description: Deficiency of thyroid hormone causing a slowing of metabolism with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance and constipation; diagnosed biochemically (raised TSH, low free T4) and easily treated with levothyroxine.
overview.detailed_description: Primary hypothyroidism is common, most often autoimmune (Hashimoto's) or iatrogenic (post-thyroidectomy/radioiodine, drugs). Symptoms are nonspecific and insidious, so diagnosis rests on thyroid function tests. Treatment is levothyroxine titrated to normalise TSH. Subclinical hypothyroidism (raised TSH, normal free T4) is managed selectively.
overview.pathophysiology: Reduced thyroid hormone output lowers basal metabolic rate across tissues; loss of negative feedback raises pituitary TSH (primary hypothyroidism). Autoimmune destruction (Hashimoto's) is the commonest mechanism.
overview.etiology: Autoimmune (Hashimoto's) thyroiditis; iatrogenic (thyroid surgery, radioiodine, external radiotherapy); drugs (amiodarone, lithium, some tyrosine-kinase inhibitors); iodine deficiency or excess; transient (postpartum/subacute thyroiditis); central (pituitary) causes are rare.
overview.natural_history: Usually chronic and progressive (autoimmune); requires lifelong replacement in most. Some transient forms recover.
overview.prognosis: Excellent with treatment; untreated severe disease can cause myxoedema and rarely myxoedema coma.

prevalence.value: Common; overt hypothyroidism affects a few percent of adults, more in women and with age; subclinical is more frequent.

incidence.value: Rises with age; much higher in women.

mortality.value: Very low with treatment; myxoedema coma has high mortality but is rare.

epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; iodine deficiency important in some regions.

risk_factors.diabetes: Type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune conditions cluster with autoimmune thyroid disease.
risk_factors.pregnancy: Postpartum thyroiditis; hypothyroidism in pregnancy needs careful management (affects the baby).
risk_factors.medications: Amiodarone, lithium, interferons, tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, iodine.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Other autoimmune disease, prior thyroid surgery/radioiodine, neck radiotherapy, Down/Turner syndromes.

symptoms.symptom: Dry skin, hair thinning, hoarse voice
Low mood / poor concentration, menstrual changes (menorrhagia)

negative_findings.why_important: Excludes primary hypothyroidism as the cause of symptoms

negative_findings.finding: No cold intolerance, normal reflexes, normal bowel habit

history_questions.question: Do you feel tired, cold, and constipated, with weight gain?
Any prior thyroid surgery/radioiodine, neck radiotherapy, or drugs like amiodarone/lithium?
Family or personal history of autoimmune/thyroid disease?
Are you pregnant or planning pregnancy?
history_questions.why_ask: Requires prompt, careful management for the baby

history_questions.question: Any neck swelling (goitre) or symptoms of other autoimmune disease?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Dry skin, coarse hair, hoarse voice
Bradycardia; delayed relaxation of ankle reflex

physical_examination.examination: Signs of complications (effusions, oedema, mental state if severe)

vital_signs.temperature: Normal or low (hypothermia in myxoedema coma)
vital_signs.blood_pressure: May have diastolic hypertension; hypotension in myxoedema coma

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Primary hypothyroidism: raised TSH with low free T4; subclinical: raised TSH, normal free T4

laboratory_tests.indication: Confirm autoimmune cause / predict progression in subclinical disease

ecg.when_needed: If bradycardia/cardiac symptoms or severe disease
ecg.findings: Sinus bradycardia, low voltage, prolonged QT in severe hypothyroidism.

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Fine-needle aspiration only for suspicious nodules

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Primary hypothyroidism: raised TSH with low free T4. Subclinical hypothyroidism: raised TSH with normal free T4 (confirm on repeat). Central hypothyroidism (rare): low/normal TSH with low free T4.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: No routine score; symptom scores are unreliable (biochemistry is definitive).

cutoff_values.value: Diagnosis and treatment thresholds are laboratory- and guideline-specific; subclinical management often considers TSH >10 mU/L, symptoms, age, and pregnancy status (NICE NG145).

differential_diagnosis.disease: Non-thyroidal illness / other causes of fatigue (anaemia, depression, diabetes)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are the thyroid tests normal with another explanation?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Normal free T4, often minimal symptoms
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the free T4 normal with only a raised TSH?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Pituitary/hypothalamic disease; TSH not appropriately raised
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_labs: Low free T4 with low/normal TSH
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is TSH low/normal despite low T4?
Is the patient drowsy/hypothermic and severely unwell?

diagnostic_questions.question: What do the thyroid function tests (TSH and free T4) show?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Raised TSH + low free T4 -> primary hypothyroidism

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you pregnant or planning pregnancy?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Positive -> prompt treatment and specialist input

next_best_question.question: Shall we check thyroid function (and antibodies), and are you pregnant or on relevant drugs?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Raised TSH/low T4 -> levothyroxine; subclinical -> selective treatment/monitor; pregnancy -> prompt management; normal TFTs -> seek other cause

next_best_test.test: TSH and free T4 (+ TPO antibodies)

next_best_test.why: Confirm subclinical results and assess associated features

red_flags.finding: Reduced consciousness, hypothermia, and severe illness (myxoedema coma)
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - admit for IV thyroid hormone, supportive care, treat precipitant/adrenal cover

red_flags.finding: Hypothyroidism in pregnancy or planning pregnancy
red_flags.immediate_action: Prompt treatment and specialist input (affects fetal development)

red_flags.finding: Suspected central hypothyroidism (low T4 with non-raised TSH)
red_flags.immediate_action: Investigate pituitary function; check cortisol before starting thyroxine

red_flags.finding: Angina worsening on starting levothyroxine (elderly/cardiac disease)
red_flags.immediate_action: Start low, go slow; cardiac review

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Myxoedema coma (emergency); hypothyroidism in pregnancy; suspected central hypothyroidism.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Diagnostic uncertainty, unusual causes, difficult-to-control disease, or suspicious thyroid nodule.

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the lifelong nature (usually), the need for adherence and monitoring.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Levothyroxine; Liothyronine. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG145.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Consistent medication timing; adequate but not excessive iodine; report symptoms of over/under-replacement.
initial_management.follow_up: TSH monitoring after dose changes and at least annually once stable; adjust dose in pregnancy promptly.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Levothyroxine, titrated to normalise TSH (and clinical response); start low and titrate slowly in the elderly or those with cardiac disease. Take on an empty stomach, consistently. Monitor TSH after ~6-8 weeks of a dose change, then periodically. Subclinical hypothyroidism: treat selectively (e.g., TSH >10, symptoms, pregnancy).

patient_education.home_advice: An underactive thyroid slows the body down, causing tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold and constipation. It is easily treated with a daily thyroxine tablet, usually for life. Take it every day on an empty stomach, and have your blood level checked as advised. Tell your doctor promptly if you become pregnant, as your dose may need increasing.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: خمول الغدة الدرقية يُبطئ الجسم فيسبّب التعب وزيادة الوزن والإحساس بالبرد والإمساك. علاجه سهل بحبة ثيروكسين يومية، غالباً مدى الحياة. تناولها يومياً على معدة فارغة، وافحص مستوى الدم كما يُنصح. أخبر طبيبك فوراً إذا حملتِ، فقد تحتاج الجرعة للزيادة.
patient_education.prevention: Adequate dietary iodine (where deficient); no primary prevention for autoimmune disease.
patient_education.warning_signs: Marked drowsiness/hypothermia, worsening chest pain on treatment, or symptoms during pregnancy.

prevention.screening: Test thyroid function in those with symptoms, other autoimmune disease, or relevant drugs; screen in pregnancy/high-risk per guidance.

evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG145; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Restore euthyroidism safely and identify reversible/central causes.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Levothyroxine; Liothyronine. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG145.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Explain consistent administration and separation from iron/calcium/antacids; correct the cause where possible.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Confirmed primary hypothyroidism with dose individualised to age, cardiac status and pregnancy
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: untreated thyrotoxicosis or uncorrected adrenal insufficiency
use_caution_if: coronary disease, arrhythmia, older/frail patient, pregnancy, or malabsorption
monitoring: TSH after initiation/dose changes and periodically; closer monitoring in pregnancy and cardiac disease

medication_options.when_to_consider: Not routine; only after specialist assessment in selected persistent cases
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: untreated thyrotoxicosis or uncorrected adrenal insufficiency
use_caution_if: coronary disease, arrhythmia, older/frail patient, pregnancy, osteoporosis, or concomitant thyroid hormone
monitoring: TSH and thyroid hormones, pulse/ECG when indicated, symptoms and bone/cardiac adverse effects

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent hospital care for suspected myxoedema coma; endocrine referral for central disease, pregnancy complexity or diagnostic uncertainty.
